summary: Static trace of what the 20F66 userland asks the kernel for on the frame path (IOMobileFramebuffer and IOSurface user-client selectors, found by following branch islands to IOConnectCall*Method in the dyld shared cache) against the project's kernel stand-ins. IOMobileFramebuffer: 63 distinct constant selectors, 16 handled by MiniIOMobileFramebuffer, 4 named only, 43 unnamed (default answers success with zeros). IOSurface: 43 selectors, 18 handled by MiniIOSurface, 4 named only, 21 unknown (default answers kIOReturnUnsupported). QuartzCore has a software-renderer path in its own strings; the donor's vtable-hook addresses match our cache. The donor's claims about software rendering and Mesa are recorded as claims about other phones. Answer: a first frame without a GPU driver is plausible, not proven; no promise of software rendering; the earliest blocker is the root delivery and dyld/launchd, not a renderer; the cheapest S24 observation is a dynamically linked test program that calls IOMobileFramebuffer/IOSurface against the stand-ins after milestone 2, with a host harness only if NAT-070 shows the panel follows the framebuffer.
evidence_category: source-review (static reading of Apple's shared cache and of donor and project sources). Nothing ran on the S24; no iOS UI; no claim about run-time behaviour of backboardd.

acceptance.1_trace: Met for the kernel interface level: selector censuses for both user clients with the stand-ins' coverage, plus the vtable-slot check for the renderer hooks. Not traced: which of the uncovered selectors backboardd/QuartzCore reach on the path to one frame (needs a run) and IOSurface traps.
acceptance.2_donor_claims: Met: section 'Established' item 5 lists donor statements (HakiOS, ios-lemonadep, y2sios) as claims about other hardware and kernels, and states what they leave open here.
acceptance.3_cheapest_observation: Met: section 'Cheapest observation, and what to prepare on the host' (no new run before a dynamic Mach-O runs; host harness conditional on NAT-070; first S24 observation; readiness criteria for milestones 4 and 5).

validation_of_the_method: The IOSurface per-export attribution reproduces the names of every selector in the stand-in's own kSurfaceMethod* enum (e.g. 5 = IOSurfaceClientSetYCbCrMatrix, 35 = ...CreateMachPortWithOptions), which cross-checks the scan against an independent source. For IOMobileFramebuffer the per-export attribution is not informative (everything lands on IOMobileFramebufferOpen) and only the selector set is used.
corrections_made_during_review: The first scan found 0 IOConnectCall hits because the cache's cross-image calls go through branch islands (adrp+add+br) that were not followed; fixed, then re-run.

A first version of the note covered IOMobileFramebuffer only; the IOSurface census was added because the task asks for IOSurface and the two stand-ins differ in how they answer unknown calls (zeros vs kIOReturnUnsupported).
limits: Only constant-selector calls through direct or island-resolved branches are seen; selectors built at run time or reached through function pointers are missed.
Selector meanings for calls the stand-ins do not name are unknown.
Donor claims are not verified here.
No scan-out evidence: whether the panel follows the loader's framebuffer is NAT-070.
